skills.trigger: Evaluating a chest X-ray in the context of blunt thoracic trauma (e.g., crush injury, MVA) to distinguish between pulmonary parenchymal injury and vascular/diaphragmatic trauma.
steps: Assess lung fields for diffuse, patchy, non-segmental airspace opacities that do not conform to anatomical lobes or vascular distributions, which are characteristic of pulmonary contusions.

Evaluate the mediastinal contour specifically for widening (>8 cm at the level of the aortic knob), loss of the aortopulmonary window, or deviation of the trachea/NG tube to rule out blunt aortic injury.
Inspect the hemidiaphragms for abnormal elevation, discontinuity, or intrathoracic herniation of abdominal contents to exclude traumatic diaphragmatic rupture.
Check costophrenic angles and lung bases for meniscus signs or layering densities to identify pleural effusions/hemothorax rather than pure parenchymal consolidation.
